lines.t: The word of the Lord came down like thunder,
“Jonah, go to Nineveh, cry out My name.”
But Jonah turned and fled from wonder,
Sailed away, escaping the flame.
The sea grew wild, the winds grew loud,
As sailors trembled, the waves bowed down.
He said, “It’s me, I’ve run from God,”
And over the side, they cast him now.
From the depths, from the deep blue sea,
Grace still calls and rescues me.
When I run, when I hide my face,
Your mercy finds me in every place.
Oh Lord, You calm the storm-tossed sea,
Your love still reaches even me.
Three days in the belly of the deep,
Jonah prayed where the dark waves creep.
“I cried to You from the pit of despair,
And You heard my voice, You answered there.”
The fish obeyed, the prophet was free,
Set on the shore with a heart made clean.
Now Jonah walked the path once denied,
To speak of judgment and mercy entwined.
From the depths, from the deep blue sea,
Grace still calls and rescues me.
When I run, when I hide my face,
Your mercy finds me in every place.
Oh Lord, You calm the storm-tossed sea,
Your love still reaches even me.
Nineveh bowed, their hearts were torn,
From the least to the king, repentance was born.
And though Jonah sat beneath the vine,
The Lord still whispered, “Mercy is Mine.”
More than wrath, more than pride,
My love for the lost will not subside.
From the depths, from the deep blue sea,
Grace still calls and rescues me.
Through the storm, through the prophet’s cry,
Your mercy reigns and will not die.
Oh Lord, You calm the storm-tossed sea,
Your love still reaches even me.
